title: Three-point ask and behavioral evidence — Carmen Alvarez
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal prep doc in advance of calibration conversation. Distills a short ask set (3 items), compact behavioral evidence tied to measurable outcomes, and a few fallback options if the primary asks aren’t workable. Keep it conversational; plan to leave copies with manager after meeting.

Three asks (priority order):
1) Compensation alignment: ask for base salary increase to market range midpoint for Senior People Ops (data attached).
   - Rationale: added scope (owning onboarding redesign + ops for two new hires in infra + running cross-functional onboarding playbook).
   - Target: $X -> justify with market comp link (CONFLUENCE-7892) and internal comp bands (JIRA-PEOPLE-412).

2) Title scope clarification: formal recognition of expanded scope (Senior -> Senior II / Lead) or explicit roadmap to promotion with milestones and timeline (6 months).
   - Rationale: I’ve been operating at the next level on project ownership and cross-team influence; need clarity to continue building external credibility.

3) Development time & coaching: commit to 1:1 coaching sessions (biweekly for 3 months) with an internal coach and 40 hours of blocked development time to lead a strategic patch (onboarding metrics & eval pipeline).

Behavioral evidence (concise bullets, examples + measurable outcomes):
- Onboarding redesign (Q4 2025 -> Feb 2026): led cross-functional working group (Eng, Growth, DS). Outcome: reduced median time-to-first-PR for new hires from 26 days -> 15 days in pilot cohort (n=9). Slide deck + pilot metrics: CONFLUENCE-7892.
- Hiring onboarding ops for infra team (Jan 2026): designed and shipped the onboarding checklist and async learning path; two hires ramped to full productivity 18% faster than forecast at 6-week checkpoint. Anecdote: Eng lead sent direct note "most improved onboarding we've had" (copied in Slack thread).
- Cross-team initiative: introduced "onboarding retro" cadence with Eng and SRE; discovered 3 systemic blockers and drove fixes: (1) infra cred distribution, (2) service sandbox access, (3) sequencing of docs. Net time saved ~2 hours/wk per manager across 5 teams (est.).
- Cost-aware ops: optimized recurring onboarding session by consolidating vendor demos -> saved ~$6k/quarter vs prior spend. Tracked in spreadsheet (see linked PR).
- Influence and representation: represented People Ops at Hiring Council (Dec 2025) and presented roadmap to execs; received follow-up invite to present onboarding metrics to Hiring Council in March.

Narrative to open with (60–90s):
"I want to align on three things that would help me keep delivering at higher impact: compensation that reflects the added scope I’ve taken on, clarity on title/level or a concrete roadmap to get there within 6 months, and structured development time/coaching so I can scale this work across teams. Quick summary of outcomes: onboarding pilot shortened ramp time by ~40%, operational changes saved recurring spend and manager time, and I've already been asked to present to Hiring Council — which I see as a signal we should make this role and pipeline more formal."

Anticipated pushbacks and suggested responses:
- "Budget constraints" -> "I understand; we can consider phased increase or a one-time bonus tied to shipping the onboarding eval pipeline by June. Also open to revisit at mid-year with OKR outcomes."
- "Title changes are slow" -> "If title isn't possible now, let's define 3 measurable milestones and timeline to get there, documented in a short promotion plan."
- "Coaching time is tight" -> "I can trial a 3-month biweekly cadence and show the ROI by the end of the trial via improved onboarding metrics; if not useful, we stop."

Fallback/scaled options (if primary asks denied):
- If base increase denied: ask for one-time retention bonus plus public recognition (liaison title on org chart) and an expanded growth plan.
- If title denied: ask for a formal 6-month promotion plan with checkpoints and a written memo outlining expectations and measures.
- If coaching denied: ask for monthly skip-level feedback sessions with a senior people leader and pairing time with Meera on program design.

Concrete examples I will pull into the meeting if needed:
- Pilot cohort table: start date, PR latency metric, ramp days saved (link: CONFLUENCE-7892).
- Slack excerpt from Eng lead praising onboarding changes (copied to appendix).
- Cost spreadsheet snapshot and vendor consolidation PR (GitHub PR #53).

Open questions I want help answering in the meeting:
- What is the current internal comp midpoint for Senior People Ops in our banding? (ask manager to surface comp comp sheet).
- Is there appetite to convert the onboarding pilot into a 3-month program with dedicated FTE time?
- What are the promotion cycle windows and what documentation is required for a level move?

Next actions (pre-meeting):
- Send this doc to manager 24 hours before meeting (planned send date: 2026-03-12).
- Attach two slides: one-page metrics summary + one slide with milestone roadmap for promotion.
- Prep 2-minute demo of the onboarding flow (local runbook) to show friction points fixed.

Post-meeting follow-ups to track (if ask accepted or partially accepted):
- Capture agreed milestones in JIRA ticket JIRA-PEOPLE-412 and link to promotion plan.
- Set calendar reminders for 6-week and 12-week check-ins; invite Meera and Noah as reviewers.
- Update CONFLUENCE-7892 with final metrics and a short retrospective doc.

Tone reminders to self:
- Be concise and outcomes-focused; managers get granular once aligned on intent.
- Use calibrated language: "I propose" vs "I demand"; give alternatives.
- Bring evidence, but don't overload — point to 1–2 strongest metrics and offer more in follow-up doc.

Quick checklist for the meeting:
- [ ] Send this doc to manager
- [ ] Add slides to calendar invite
- [ ] Bring printed one-pager (or screen share)
- [ ] Set 30-minute meeting (not 15)

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to breathe. Focus on system changes not personal validation.
- If manager pushes purely on budget, emphasize ROI: reduced manager time + faster ramp = lower time-to-impact for revenue/engineering projects.

End of scratchpad.
